elements.element: No MFN / right-to-match obligation imposed on Customer (disclosure duty)
elements.evidence: "Customer need not disclose ... any more favourable commercial offer it receives"

elements.element: No obligation on Customer to match a more favourable offer for Vendor
elements.evidence: "need not disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer"

elements.element: No condition precedent restricting Customer from engaging another provider
elements.evidence: "Before engaging another provider, Customer need not disclose and match" — lead-in is left without any operative duty

elements.element: MFN scope limited to a defined product
elements.evidence: clause refers generally to "any more favourable commercial offer"; no defined product
no duration stated in Section 7.2 as revised
no comparison or carve-out language present

reasons: The single operator flip ("must disclose" → "need not disclose") removes the disclosure and match duty, so no MFN/right-to-match obligation runs against Customer, satisfying the locked preferred level.
Change is minimal: one short phrase replaced rather than a clause rewrite or deletion, and no fallback mechanics (defined product, 12-month term, carve-outs) were imported.

Intent preserved: no undefined terms or contradictions introduced; the residual lead-in "Before engaging another provider" is now merely descriptive and consistent with Section 12.3's acknowledgement of no most-favoured-customer commitment.
Fallback is not satisfied on its own terms, but that is irrelevant because the preferred position is fully met.
